channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Prazo para entrada em vigor de novas tarifas dos EUA termina em dez dias; governo espera por mais uma reunião de negociação
item.description: The deadline for the U.S. to decide on implementing additional tariffs on Brazilian products is July 15, with only ten days remaining. The Brazilian government is seeking to reverse part of the U.S. proposal to raise total tariffs to 37.5% through a 'roadmap' presented in technical talks, including a virtual meeting last Thursday with the U.S. Trade Representative. Although Lula’s advisors acknowledge they no longer expect a full reversal, they aim to exhaust negotiations before the deadline.

item.title: De volta a Brasília, Flamengo testará craques visando retorno pós-Copa
item.description: Flamengo will face Olimpia of Paraguay in a pre-season friendly at Arena Mané Garrincha in Brasília on July 17 at 8 p.m., as part of their preparation to resume the national calendar after the 2026 World Cup break. The match, organized by Metrópoles Sports, will have tickets available via Ticket and Go starting at R$ 59, with players such as Rossi, Jorginho and Samuel Lino expected to play.

item.title: O que trava palanques de Lula e Flávio em Minas a 3 meses da eleição
item.description: Three months out from the election, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro have yet to secure electoral slates in Minas Gerais due to rejections from key allies and internal disagreements. Lula struggles after Rodrigo Pacheco’s refusal and Marília Campos’ unwillingness to run for governor, while Flávio awaits Cleitinho Azevedo’s decision, with the PL exploring internal options as the right-wing remains fragmented in the state.

item.title: Datafolha: Tarcísio lidera disputa pelo governo de SP com 46%; Haddad tem 30%
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas leads the race for São Paulo governor with 46% voting intention, followed by Fernando Haddad at 30%, according to a Datafolha poll. In valid votes simulation, Tarcísio reaches 52% versus Haddad's 34%, but the margin of error prevents confirming a first-round victory. The survey was conducted between July 1 and 3 with 1,608 voters across 71 municipalities.

item.title: Datafolha: aprovação da gestão Tarcísio em SP permanece em 45%
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' approval rating in São Paulo remains stable at 45% rating his management as good or excellent, according to a Datafolha poll released on May 5. His overall performance as governor was approved by 63% of respondents, with 32% disapproving and 6% undecided. Regular (32%), bad/terrible (20%), and don't know (3%) ratings showed minimal changes from the previous survey.

item.title: 'Não vou alimentar conflito', diz vereadora citada em vídeo de Michelle
item.description: Fortaleza councilwoman Priscila Costa (PL-CE) released a video stating she 'will not fuel any kind of conflict' between Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro, after being sidelined in the Ceará Senate race. Her decision to remain neutral has intensified the rift between the former first lady and the senator. Costa aims to avoid taking sides in the internal PL dispute in Ceará.

item.title: Vozinha fecha participação na Copa com 24,3 milhões de seguidores
item.description: Cape Verdean goalkeeper Josimar Dias, nicknamed Vozinha, ended his 2026 World Cup journey with 24.3 million Instagram followers, surpassing the national teams of France, Argentina, England, Spain, Germany, Italy, and Uruguay, as well as political figures like Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Luciano Huck. His social media surge began after Cape Verde's opening draw against Spain, amplified by a call-to-action from CazéTV. Though behind only Brazil’s national team (26.8 million) and celebrities like Neymar, Anitta, and Virgínia Fonseca, Vozinha emerged as one of the most followed athletes in the tournament.

item.title: Jhonatan de Jesus é uma síntese do derretimento das instituições
item.description: Jhonatan de Jesus is portrayed as a symbol of the erosion of Brazilian institutions, having become a TCU minister through political nomination by Arthur Lira and Centrão support, despite lacking experience and having a record of unspent parliamentary amendments in Roraima. His background includes strong advocacy for Daniel Vorcaro and Banco Master interests, as well as attacks on the Central Bank, raising serious concerns about his suitability for a role overseeing public accounts.

item.title: Flávio embarca aos EUA para audiência sobre tarifaço
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) traveled to Washington, D.C., to attend a U.S. government public hearing on the proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, where he registered to speak against the measure. He advocates for suspending the tariffs, launching bilateral U.S.-Brazil trade talks, reducing regulatory and tax burdens on payment companies, and freeing Brazil from Mercosul constraints to negotiate directly with the United States.

item.title: Bruno Guimarães liga o alerta e pede atenção contra Haaland na Copa
item.description: Bruno Guimarães, Brazil's assist leader in the 2026 World Cup, warned that Erling Haaland must be tightly marked, calling him one of the world's best strikers. He said his role will depend on who replaces the injured Paquetá, possibly shifting to a more defensive duty, and described the Norway match as tight and challenging.

item.title: GCM prende dois suspeitos de roubar celulares na Avenida Paulista
item.description: The Metropolitan Civil Guard (GCM) arrested two suspects for cellphone robbery on Paulista Avenue after a pursuit against traffic. The suspects were identified by the victim and taken to the 78th Police District. The operation highlights the Tarcísio de Freitas administration’s focus on curbing the 'glass-breaking gang,' which heightens public insecurity during the election year.

item.title: Pivô da crise entre Michelle e Flávio faz apelo por união
item.description: City councilwoman Priscila Costa (PL-CE), identified as the focal point of tension between Michelle Bolsonaro and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, released a video urging unity among the right-wing and denying any intention to fuel conflict. She emphasized the need to maintain cohesion within the Bolsonarist base ahead of the 2026 political challenges.

item.title: Ancelotti indica possível substituto de Paquetá e explica critério
item.description: Brazil's head coach Carlo Ancelotti stated there is no direct replacement for the injured Lucas Paquetá and will select a substitute based on tactical needs against Norway, mentioning Danilo, Gabriel, Matheus Cunha, Éderson, Douglas Santos, and Martinelli as options. He also confirmed Raphinha is progressing well in recovery and may play limited minutes off the bench.

item.title: PSol aciona MPSP contra Tarcísio por propaganda da Sabesp
item.description: The PSol filed a representation with the MPSP against Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, alleging improper propaganda of Sabesp on social media following its 2024 privatization, using public resources to benefit a private entity. The party claims the governor's posts about the company's works and investments violate impartiality and confidentiality duties, and requests an investigation into potential favoritism toward Sabesp's image before investors, with referral to the CVM, MPF, and TCE-SP.

item.title: Richarlison volta a citar disputa de mansão com Flávio: "Me tomaram"
item.description: Richarlison reiterated that he lost a mansion in Angra dos Reis valued at around R$10 million due to a legal dispute over possession versus property rights, stating he has not been reimbursed. He reposted a video from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro showing the property, commenting 'Me tomaram'. Although Bolsonaro is not a party to the case, he was listed as a witness by Richarlison’s lawyers in 2022.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro responde críticas por elogiar iniciativa de Lula: ‘acima de ideologia’
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro defended her praise for the National Policy of Bilingual Education for the Deaf launched by the Lula government, stating that disability advocacy is 'above ideology or party'. She also claimed the initiative was developed during her husband Jair Bolsonaro’s presidency but delayed by a judicial action. Her comments come amid family tensions with her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and backlash from the right for applauding a policy from the Workers’ Party government.

item.title: “13 x 22”: camisas da Seleção na Copa são tragadas para a polarização
item.description: Brazil's victory over Japan in the World Cup, with Martinelli (number 22) scoring after Danilo's (number 13) error, was politicized by right-wing figures who linked the jersey numbers to the PT's (13) and PL's (22) ballot numbers, despite no evidence of the players' political affiliations.

item.title: Moraes manda apreender 11 armas de Bolsonaro; leia a lista
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the seizure of 11 firearms belonging to former President Jair Bolsonaro, revoking his gun possession rights and collector’s certificate while maintaining his house arrest for health reasons. The order includes a Glock pistol seized during a June 15 traffic stop in Brasília, carried by Bolsonaro’s security aide. Bolsonaro’s defense has 48 hours to surrender the weapons to the Federal Police.

item.title: Após decisão, influencer volta a atacar nordestinos: "Vão comer pombo"
item.description: Influencer Gabriel Silva reacted to a court decision suspending his Instagram profile by attacking the judge, insulting Northeastern Brazilians, and claiming his videos are designed to go viral, including stating that those who keep voting for Lula 'will eat pigeon'.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro rebate críticas por elogios a projeto de Lula
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro defended the National Policy for Bilingual Education of the Deaf (Pnebs), praising the initiative from Lula’s government while asserting its origins trace back to the Bolsonaro administration. She stressed that the deaf community’s cause must transcend ideology and party, citing Jair Bolsonaro’s approval of the Amália Barros Law — proposed by a PT lawmaker — as an example of prioritizing public good over political divides.

item.title: Haddad prepara convenção em Ribeirão Preto no fim do mês
item.description: Lula will attend the PT convention in Ribeirão Preto on July 25 to formally launch Fernando Haddad's candidacy for governor of São Paulo, aiming to strengthen the party's presence in the state's interior. The event coincides with the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential pre-candidacy, with Lula showing strategic support for Haddad after persuading him to run despite his initial reluctance.

item.title: PT aprova destino de R$ 127 milhões para campanha de Lula em 2026
item.description: The Workers' Party approved the allocation of R$127 million from the Special Campaign Financing Fund for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 2026 re-election campaign, representing 20.64% of the R$615.3 million the party received this year. The remaining funds were distributed among candidacies for the Chamber of Deputies (R$264.9 million), state governments (R$71.9 million), Federal Senate (R$62 million), state and district legislative assemblies (R$50 million), and a reserve fund (R$39 million).

item.title: Michelle diz que pauta de surdos está acima de ideologia
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro stated that advocacy for the deaf community transcends ideology or political party, after praising the launch of the Pnebs by the Lula government. She emphasized that the initiative was initiated during Jair Bolsonaro’s administration but delayed by a judicial dispute, and cited the sanctioning of the Amália Barros Law as an example of prioritizing public benefit over partisan authorship. Her remarks drew criticism from Bolsonaro supporters and come amid public tensions with her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: O objetivo de Kassab ao insistir em chapa puro-sangue do PSD ao Planalto
item.description: Gilberto Kassab is pushing for a pure PSD ticket for the presidency, primarily aiming to strengthen the party’s congressional caucuses by leveraging TV exposure to boost ballot recognition. The selection of Ronaldo Caiado as presidential candidate and Kassab as running mate reflects Caiado’s weak polling, which blocked alliances with other parties. Although the ticket’s electoral prospects are seen as low, some internally hope that scandals involving Flávio Bolsonaro could swing voters toward the PSD duo.

item.title: Ao lado de Zema, Girão oficializa pré-candidatura ao governo do Ceará
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) officially launched his pre-candidacy for Governor of Ceará at an event in Caucaia, attended by former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, who is backing the candidacy. The event was part of the sixth edition of the 'Ceará Tem Jeito' movement, discussing health, education, public safety, and economic development. Girão’s candidacy still requires confirmation at the Novo party’s state convention, scheduled for August.

item.title: Wilson Pedroso na Crusoé: Flávio tem a senha; Michelle tem conexão
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll reveals that, despite the crisis surrounding the Bolsonaro family, Flávio Bolsonaro remains the base’s authorized choice for 2026, while Michelle Bolsonaro maintains strong voter connection without being seen as a natural candidate. The survey highlights a key challenge for Bolsonarism: Flávio’s legitimacy endures, but public exposure of the crisis complicates his path to uncontested candidacy.

item.title: “Bolsonaro está ciente de tudo o que se passa aqui fora”, diz Carluxo
item.description: Former councilman Carlos Bolsonaro (PL), pre-candidate for the Senate from Santa Catarina, visited former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest and stated that the latter is aware of external political developments. Carlos criticized the restrictions imposed by the STF in a social media post, defending his father's freedom.

item.title: Duas bombeiras impediram um incêndio ainda maior no clã Bolsonaro
item.description: Governor Celina Leão and Senator Damares Alves convinced Michelle Bolsonaro to stay in the PL party and run in local elections, despite her initial intention to leave the party and abandon her Senate bid. Her decision to remain is seen as vital for the PL, particularly due to her appeal among female and evangelical voters, though her ongoing rift with Bolsonaro’s sons continues to create family and political tensions.

item.title: O medo mudou de lado: por que isso pode ser bom para Lula?
item.description: Fear in Brazilian politics has shifted sides, moving from being a dominant tool of the opposition to also influencing the government camp, which could benefit Lula by forcing a realignment of narratives and reducing excessive polarization. This inversion suggests the electorate is more open to substantive debates, allowing the president to advance social and economic reconstruction agendas without being constantly held hostage by culture war narratives. Thus, fear, once used against him, may now serve as a catalyst for more stable and legitimate governance.

item.title: O silêncio de Carlos e Jair Renan sobre o vídeo que rachou a família
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro and Jair Renan Bolsonaro remained silent regarding the video in which Michelle Bolsonaro accused Flávio Bolsonaro of disrespect and attempting to exclude her from the party, choosing not to escalate the family conflict. While Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro are engaged in an open dispute with the former first lady, the two younger sons have focused on their respective pre-campaigns — Jair Renan in Balneário Camboriú and Carlos for the Senate — without commenting publicly on the incident.

item.title: Michelle avisou Jair Bolsonaro sobre ataques a Flávio, dizem aliadas
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro informed her husband, Jair Bolsonaro, about her decision to release a video accusing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreatment and humiliation, and announced she would step down as head of PL Mulher. She stated that all her actions were coordinated with the former president, who thus endorses her campaign against their son. The family rift has damaged Flávio’s campaign, particularly among female voters, per an AtlasIntel/Boomberg poll.

item.title: Após elogiar política de Lula, Michelle fala em pauta 'acima de ideologia'
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro praised a policy launched by the Lula government and reiterated that advocacy for the deaf community's agenda should be above ideology or party. She stated that this cause is nonpartisan and deserves support regardless of political affiliation.

item.title: Mulher na vice de Flávio vira consenso após crise com Michelle, mas perfil expõe disputa no PL
item.description: The selection of a woman as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate (PL-RJ) has become a consensus following the crisis with Michelle Bolsonaro, aiming to reduce female voter rejection. However, internal PL debate persists between ideological figures (like Bia Kicis and Júlia Zanatta) and more technical, moderate profiles (such as Daniella Marques). Pressure mounted after Michelle's video accusing Flávio of humiliation and Paulo Figueiredo's controversial remarks about women voters.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro tenta conter repercussão negativa após elogio a programa de Lula
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro sought to mitigate backlash after praising Lula's bilingual education program for the deaf, stating that disability advocacy transcends ideology and that the policy originated under Bolsonaro's government but was delayed by judicial action. She cited Jair Bolsonaro's signing of the Amália Barros Law — authored by a PT lawmaker — as proof of merit-based evaluation regardless of party affiliation. The post responded to criticism from Bolsonaro's base, which accused her of betrayal, amid internal PL tensions, including her public dispute with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and her removal from leadership of PL Women.

item.title: Grupos sociais preparam ato por procuradora que acusa expoentes da velha Lava Jato de ‘perseguição’
item.description: Human rights groups and social organizations are preparing a show of support for prosecutor Margaret Matos de Carvalho, accused of diverting R$6.2 million from a Banco Itaú agreement with the Labor Public Prosecutor's Office. She denies the allegations, claiming she is a victim of political persecution by former Lava Jato prosecutors, including Deltan Dallagnol and Diogo Castor de Mattos, due to her public support for Lula during his imprisonment. Margaret asserts the funds were used in line with the MPT’s institutional mission and that she was denied administrative defense.

item.title: Governo Lula decide jogar parado sobre barraco público entre Flávio e Michelle
item.description: Lula's campaign chose to remain passive amid the public feud between Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro, believing the internal conflict within the Bolsonaro camp benefits the president without requiring direct intervention. Allies expect the family rift to harm Flávio's appeal among female voters, potentially boosting Lula's support in that demographic.

item.title: 62% dos brasileiros dizem ter orgulho de vestir a camisa da seleção
item.description: A survey by Instituto Locomotiva in partnership with QuestionPro shows that 62% of Brazilians feel proud to wear the Brazilian national team jersey, with higher support among right-wing voters (68%) and left-wing voters (65%). Despite the jersey’s recent association with right-wing political demonstrations, intent to wear it during matches remains high across the political spectrum: 93% of right-wing and 92% of left-wing voters plan to wear the jersey, while rejection is low (5% and 6%, respectively). The poll surveyed 1,030 people nationwide from June 2 to 8, 2026, with a margin of error of 3.1 percentage points.

item.title: 46% das indústrias podem rever investimentos com fim da 6 X 1
item.description: Nearly half of Brazilian industries may revise their investment plans if the workweek is reduced from 44 to 40 hours under the proposed end of the 6x1 schedule, according to a CNI report released in July 2026. The survey shows 73% of companies oppose the reduction and 97% would be affected, mainly due to rising operational costs. The PEC, approved by the Chamber in May 2026, awaits Senate vote, with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre indicating a possible delay until after the October elections.

item.title: Na mira de tribunais de conta estaduais, ‘Palantir brasileira’ chega ao radar de fundos dos EUA
item.description: Brazilian company Pax AI, which provides AI-powered video monitoring for public safety and is compared to Palantir, is under investigation by the state audit courts of Goiás, Paraná, and São Paulo for million-reais contracts awarded without bidding. State deputy Arilson Chiorato (PT-PR) has submitted complaints to U.S. investors Benchmark and Greenoaks, which have invested around 40 million reais in the firm, warning of transparency risks and personal data violations. The company, formerly Paladium, changed its name amid scrutiny but claims the rebranding is unrelated to the investigations.

item.title: 70% defendem punir adolescentes como adultos, diz Datafolha
item.description: A June 2026 Datafolha survey shows 70% of Brazilians support trying juvenile offenders as adults, up 5 points since 2022. Support is majority across all religious groups and varies by presidential vote intention: 81% among Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) supporters and 61% among Lula (PT) supporters. Drug use prohibition also has broad support at 85%, within the margin of error compared to 2022.

item.title: Celina diz que resposta sobre candidatura de Michelle virá em agosto
item.description: The governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão (PP), stated that former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro is likely to run for the Senate in 2026, but an official response will only come in August. She said Michelle is taking time to care for herself and her husband, Jair Bolsonaro, but remains confident in her candidacy. Since Michelle stepped down from PL Mulher leadership, speculation has grown about her political future, including a public disagreement with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Cristo Redentor e Torre de TV ganham cores dos EUA no Dia da Independência
item.description: Four Brazilian monuments — Christ the Redeemer, the Estaiada Bridge, the Mário de Andrade Library, and the TV Tower — will be lit in red, white, and blue to celebrate the 250th anniversary of U.S. Independence as part of the Freedom 250 campaign. Despite the symbolic gesture of friendship, the moment is marked by commercial tension, as the U.S. threatens to impose 25% punitive tariffs on Brazilian imports over alleged discriminatory practices. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and influencer Paulo Figueiredo traveled to the U.S. to participate in the USTR public hearing and advocate against the proposed tariff.

item.title: Ancelotti prepara escalação inédita para jogo do Brasil contra a Noruega
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti is preparing an unprecedented lineup for Brazil against Norway in the 2026 World Cup round of 16 due to Lucas Paquetá's injury. Danilo Santos and Ederson are the top candidates for the vacant spot, with Raphinha returning to training and Neymar possibly coming on in the second half. The match will be played on Sunday, the 5th, at 5 PM at the New York and New Jersey Stadium, broadcast across Globo, SBT, SporTV, N Sports, GE TV (Globoplay), and CazéTV.

item.title: Após elogiar ação de Lula, Michelle fala em pauta acima de ideologia
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro praised the National Policy of Bilingual Education for the Deaf (Pnebs) launched by the Lula government, stating that advocating for the deaf community's agenda is 'above any ideology or party'. The statement comes amid a family rift with her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, after she alleged feeling humiliated and disrespected in a phone call about party strategizing.

item.title: Inveja da vagina (por Fernanda Hamann)
item.description: The article analyzes the misogynistic statements of Brazilian fugitive blogger Paulo Figueiredo, who claimed single women vote poorly and married women merely imitate their husbands' votes. It argues that his rhetoric reflects an unconscious 'penis envy' inverted — what Karen Horney termed 'vagina envy' — stemming from men's inability to gestate and thus uncertainty about biological paternity, which fuels efforts to control women's bodies through abortion laws and patriarchal norms. The piece links this psyche to Bolsonarist extremism and figures like Nick Fuentes, who advocate abolishing women's suffrage.

item.title: Lula faz 101 anúncios em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Lula made 101 announcements of works and investments between January and June 2026, intensifying his agenda in the two months before the electoral blackout period, which begins on July 4. The most prioritized themes were health (28), infrastructure (20), and education (11), while public security had only 4 announcements. He concentrated his visits in the Federal District (32), São Paulo (18), Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Bahia, with only one visit to the North (Manaus) in 2026.

item.title: Michelle explica apoio a política do governo Lula
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro explained that her support for the National Policy of Bilingual Education for the Deaf, launched by the Lula government, has no political motivation and is aligned with her historical work in inclusion. The statement came after she faced criticism for backing a policy from the Workers' Party government.

item.title: Relatório do Senado cita demora no atendimento a ‘mártir’ do bolsonarismo
item.description: A Senate Human Rights Commission report highlights delays in medical care for Clériston Pereira da Cunha, known as 'Clezão', a Bolsonaro ally imprisoned for the January 8 attacks who died of a heart attack in November 2023 at the Papuda prison. Despite suffering from serious health conditions and receiving a favorable opinion from the Prosecutor-General’s Office for provisional release in September 2023, Minister Alexandre de Moraes did not rule on the request. His defense and family claim the delayed medical response contributed to his death, and the case has resurfaced after the report was shared with the STF, CNJ, MP, and IACHR.

item.title: Pobreza é associada à preguiça por 40% dos brasileiros, diz Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha survey shows that 40% of Brazilians now link poverty to laziness, nearly double the 22% in 2022, while 58% still attribute poverty to lack of equal opportunities — down from 76% in 2022. Perceptions vary sharply by income, occupation, and presidential vote: business owners (56%) and Flávio Bolsonaro supporters (52%) are most likely to blame laziness, while Lula voters (28%) and youth aged 16–24 (22%) are least likely.

item.title: Jhon Arias, do Palmeiras, é o melhor do 'Brasileirão na Copa' após a 2ª fase; veja ranking
item.description: Jhon Arias of Palmeiras led the 'Brasileirão na Copa' ranking after the second round by scoring Colombia's winning goal against Ghana, becoming the only Brasileirão player to directly contribute to a goal in this stage. Prior to him, Gustavo Gómez, Damián Bobadilla, and Junior Alonso topped the ranking for their defensive performances in Paraguay's penalty shootout win over Germany. Negative highlights included Alan Franco and Lucas Paquetá, whose injury limited his involvement.
